subject: Renewal pricing: performance credits, prorated top-up, and invoice timing
messages:
From: Claire Zhou <czhou@solacehealth.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Solace Health Procurement <procurement@solacehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + mid-contract capacity bump — questions on billing and credits

Hi Lukas,

Quick note from our side — we expect production usage to grow by ~30% over the next quarter and would like to discuss a mid-contract top-up while keeping our renewal co-term in March. Procurement wants clarity on how Redwood will prorate the add-on (invoice timing and crediting), and our platform team asked whether we can get performance-linked credits if latency or availability targets slip during the burst window.

Contract details: current term ends 2027-03-15, committed units 120k tokens/month. Looking for options that avoid a separate annual invoice cycle.

Can you outline feasible paths and any documentation you’ll need for Procurement/Legal so we can move quickly?

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Zhou
Head of Platform Engineering
Solace Health

--
Attachment: usage-forecast-q4.csv (CSV stub referenced)

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhou <czhou@solacehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + mid-contract capacity bump — questions on billing and credits

Hi Claire — thanks for the context and the forecast. Copied Ben and Irene from commercial/support so we can align contract/pricing + operational risk. High level, there are three pragmatic paths:

1) Proportional top-up (fastest) — immediate add-on invoice for the delta (prorated to the end of your current term) + automatic roll into renewal. No change to unit price.

2) Staged top-up with invoice smoothing — split the incremental cost into monthly installments (2–3 months) to avoid a single large invoice; we can offer a modest one-time uplift discount (5%) if Solace commits to keeping the top-up for the remainder of the term.

3) Performance-credit tranche + commitment — tie a portion of the add-on to an SLO-backed credit (example: sustained 95th percentile latency exceedance during peak hours triggers credit up to 8% of that add-on invoice). This requires us to align on monitoring windows and an SLA playbook; I’ve attached a sample calculator and a draft addendum.

Deliverables we can send immediately: short amendment (billing schedule + prorate table), SLA-credit addendum (template), and a worksheet showing monthly invoice impact. Attached: proposal-delta-v1.pdf, SLA-credit-calculator.xlsx.

If Procurement wants DocuSign we’ll prepare the amendment for signature; if Legal wants to redline the addendum we can accept tracked changes. What’s your preferred procurement timeframe?

— Lukas
Lukas Meyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lukas_meyer@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 11:23:00 -0800
Subject: internal: negotiation levers for Solace top-up

Lukas / Irene — quick internal note before I respond to Procurement:

- Offer structure idea: Give Solace two-month installment + 5% one-time top-up discount (option 2) OR a slightly higher discount (8%) if they accept a 6-month amortization and a modest minimum additional commit (>= 25% increase).
- For performance credits (option 3) suggest capping exposure at 8% of the incremental invoice and require Solace to run our agent/observability hook for the measurement window. That reduces adjudication disputes.
- We should be flexible on net-30 for the add-on; the renewal invoice can remain standard terms.

I’ll draft a Word amendment with both billing options and the SLA-credit addendum marked as Appendix A. We should keep the DocuSign envelope ready but only populate the final dollar amounts after client picks a path. Internal links: pricing playbook (https://internal.redwood/pricing-playbook/topup-guides)

— Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal + mid-contract capacity bump — questions on billing and credits

Claire — appreciate the quick turn. Based on Procurement and our internal guidance, here’s a concrete offer for your review:

Option A (recommended) — Staged top-up, 2-month installment
- Delta: +36k units/month (30% growth)
- Billing: split the incremental charge into two monthly invoices; first invoice dated Nov 15 (net-30), second invoice dated Dec 15 (net-30)
- One-time uplift discount: 5% applied to the incremental charges
- No change to the existing renewal date; add-on rolls into March renewal
- Attachments: Word amendment (editable) + SLA-credit addendum as Appendix A

Option B — Amortized, higher discount
- Delta: +36k units/month
- Billing: amortize incremental cost across 6 months, one invoice per month (net-30)
- One-time uplift discount: 8% on incremental charges, requires a minimum 25% sustained increase commit
- Requires separate amendment; will impact renewal true-up calculations

Performance credits (optional add-on)
- Cap: credits up to 8% of the incremental add-on invoice for sustained SLA misses (95th pct latency); requires our monitoring hooks and agreed windows (we’ve included a sample calculator).

Next steps: I attached the Word amendment with both Option A/B and the SLA-credit addendum. If Procurement confirms PO SH-2026-4498 and signs, I’ll upload a DocuSign envelope (link below) and we’ll populate final amounts.

DocuSign (pre-populated envelope ready): https://www.docusign.com/secure/embeddedSigning?token=abc123-solace

Please let me know which option you prefer and whether Procurement wants the two-invoice split or six-month amortization. Happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow.

Best,
Lukas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lukas_meyer@redwood.com
